title: Sévaré Airport Endures Six-Night Bombardment as Mali's Army Confronts Dioura Hostage Crisis
detail: By Monday, September 21, 2026, Sévaré airport had endured six consecutive nights of JNIM shelling. A local resident who visited Sévaré's hospital told Reuters he saw roughly 40 wounded Malian soldiers and Russian Africa Corps personnel there; Russian troops were no longer visible around Sévaré by Monday. More than 100 soldiers taken hostage in the September 10 Dioura attack remained unaccounted for, and Mali's military has not disclosed the outcome of the retaliatory operation it said lasted more than a week. Reuters' roundup, citing security and diplomatic sources, marks the first consolidated public accounting of a two-week span of losses that rank among the heaviest reported for Mali's army and its Africa Corps allies since the war began, compounding pressure from JNIM's parallel blockade of Bamako.
